issues.description: The problem specification and UML define Rideable.messageOnRide() as a no-argument method returning a String (and the problem text expects returns like "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"). The template Main calls r.messageOnRide() without arguments. However, the solution implementation declares Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) (and Pig/Seal implement the method with a String parameter and include "with <equipment>" in the return). This parameter mismatch will cause compile errors or confusion: students following the problem/template will implement a no-arg messageOnRide(), but the provided solution uses a different signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable API consistent with the problem statement and template by changing Rideable.messageOnRide to a no-argument method (String messageOnRide()). Update the solution implementations (Pig and Seal) to implement the no-arg method and return the expected string format "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if the equipment parameter is intended, update the problem statement UML and the template Main (calls) to include the equipment parameter; however, the cleaner fix is to remove the equipment parameter so the interface matches the exercise description.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Rideable.messageOnRide() method with no parameters (returning a String like "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"), but the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and implements it in Pig and Seal with the extra equipment parameter and different returned text. This mismatch in the method signature and expected usage creates a direct compilation/usage conflict (e.g., Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no argument) and prevents students from mapping the problem's API to the provided solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable API consistent with the problem statement and template: change Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) to messageOnRide() returning String, and update Pig and Seal implementations to implement messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if an equipment parameter is intended, update the problem statement and template usage (Main and description) to document and call messageOnRide(String equipment).
